headline: Photosynthesis converts sunlight into food—plants capture light and build themselves from air and water
universal_truth: Energy must be captured before it can be used; all value starts with some form of harvest
fun_facts: Plants produce all the oxygen you breathe as a byproduct of photosynthesis
A single tree can absorb about 48 pounds of carbon dioxide per year
Chlorophyll reflects green light, which is why plants appear green—they use red and blue light
discussion_questions: What 'sunlight' do you capture and convert into value?
Where does your energy ultimately come from?
What inputs do you transform into outputs?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Plants are solar-powered factories. They capture photons from the sun, pull carbon dioxide from air, draw water from soil, and build themselves—sugar, cellulose, wood. From light and air, they create matter. This is photosynthesis: the foundation of almost all life.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: All food energy on Earth traces back to photosynthesis. Plants capture sunlight; everything else just transfers that captured energy. What does this teach us about value creation?
cliff.prompt: What does photosynthesis teach about value?

options.text: Value must first be captured from some source—before you can transform or transfer energy, someone or something must harvest it from the environment
options.response: Yes. Plants are primary producers—they capture energy that then flows through all life. Understanding the source of value shows where prosperity begins.
They're food, but more fundamentally they're energy capturers—the foundation everything else depends on...

q1.title: Light to Matter
q1.script: Photosynthesis uses light energy to break water molecules, releasing oxygen. The hydrogen combines with carbon dioxide to form glucose—sugar. Light becomes matter. The tree's wood was once sunlight and air.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Light to Matter"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Primary Production
q2.script: Plants are primary producers—they create food from non-food. Everything else is secondary: eating plants, eating plant-eaters, decomposing remains. All energy traces back to photosynthetic capture.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Your Energy Source
q3.script: You run on captured sunlight too—just filtered through food chains. The energy in your breakfast was sunlight, captured by plants, perhaps eaten by animals, now powering your thoughts. You're solar-powered.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Energy must be captured before it can be used. All value starts with some form of harvest. Know where your energy comes from.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 241. Tomorrow, we'll explore how bodies make energy—metabolism. Until then, trace your food back to its sunlight source.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Energy Tracing - Where Does Yours Come From?
growTrack.learning_objective: Trace energy sources to their origins
growTrack.activity: Pick something you consumed today—food, fuel, electricity. Trace it back: where did that energy originally come from? Most paths lead to sunlight captured by plants. Understanding energy sources reveals hidden dependencies.
